content.title: Will the Person Who Left Home Smiling This Morning Return by Evening?
content.subtitle: Carry your divine shield of protection into this city of concrete and death.
content.body:
In the evening, a young motorcyclist may be standing at Bijoy Sarani or near Kuril Flyover, the exhaustion of an entire day visible on his face, yet driven by the urgency to return home. Moments later, a reckless bus speeding from behind may strike him violently, and that young life may be extinguished on the asphalt road.

On the Saidabad–Jatrabari route, a bag of carefully purchased fruits for a child may slip from a father’s hand as he is crushed beneath a vehicle. On the Airport Road, the dreams of two students may be shattered in an instant amid reckless bus racing, leaving behind bloodstained ID cards and scattered books and notebooks. On the Dhaka–Mawa Expressway, an ambulance carrying a family home after taking a sick relative for treatment may lose control, returning the entire family as lifeless bodies. Or, on a foggy highway, a group of workers may meet their final breath when their vehicle crashes into a disabled truck.

The Statistics of Lives Lost on the Asphalt

Statistics from the Jatri Kalyan Samity and Road Safety Foundation indicate that this deadly road claimed more than 8,000 lives in just the past year. On average, 20 to 25 families bid farewell to their loved ones with smiles in the morning, only to receive their lifeless bodies by the end of the day. Behind every accident lies a shattered family and lost dreams. And silently, the asphalt roads grow heavier with the unspoken grief of those left behind.

The Limits of Human Caution

You may follow every traffic law perfectly. You may walk carefully along the pavement. Yet, when a speeding truck with failed brakes suddenly approaches from behind or a reckless bus comes rushing from the wrong direction, all your personal precautions can become helpless in an instant.

When every worldly means and human calculation reaches its limit, who remains the ultimate refuge for a believer? Standing before such extreme uncertainty, our beloved Prophet ﷺ taught us an unseen and unbreakable shield of divine protection.

The Ultimate Shield of Divine Protection

When leaving home and stepping onto the uncertain roads of this world, the Messenger of Allah ﷺ taught his Ummah a powerful means of seeking protection. Through it, the Lord of the Throne places His servant under His divine care:

بِسْمِ اللَّهِ، تَوَكَّلْتُ عَلَى اللَّهِ، وَلَا حَوْلَ وَلَا قُوَّةَ إِلَّا بِاللَّهِ

Meaning: “In the name of Allah, I place my complete trust in Allah. There is no power to avoid harm or attain goodness except through Allah.”

A hadith mentions that when a servant recites these words upon leaving home, a voice from the unseen calls out: “You have been guided, you have been sufficed, and you have been protected.”

The Shaytan then retreats from him in despair. Another Shaytan says to him, “How can you influence a person who has been guided, sufficed, and protected?” (Sunan Abi Dawud: 5095; Jami‘ at-Tirmidhi: 3426)

Complete Security Lies in the Sunnah

Every Sunnah of the Prophet ﷺ is not merely a custom or ritual. Rather, in this uncertain and fragile life, it carries divine tranquility and a means of protection. At the end of the day, what greater blessing could there be than returning home safely, away from countless dangers and uncertainties, and seeing the gentle smiles of those we love?

Likewise, the Sunnah of entering the home with salam after returning from outside brings blessings and mercy into the household and helps keep away harm and discord.

So, starting today, can we make these often-forgotten Sunnahs an inseparable part of our lives?
